clue.text: Stick firmly together at this place, following County

indicators.note: one thing following another places the place-word after the county abbreviation

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for county
a plain synonym for at this place

explanation.surface: Instructions to bind something tightly here, next to a county boundary marker perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together as a unified mass, a verb matching stick firmly together.

clue.text: Preach on rocky headland

indicators.note: rocky suggests something unsteady and shaken up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sermonising while standing on a rugged clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word placing the preacher, but its letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Horn is the famous headland at the southern tip of South America.

clue.text: See 1
Spend time in the country with reportedly dull girl?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: dull is rusty, and Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone off on a rural retreat with a reportedly boring young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to go to live or stay in the countryside, away from town.

clue.text: Band in joint agreed to

blocks.note: the wrist is a joint; 'in' merely places it
to let is to allow, i.e. agreed to

explanation.surface: A strap or brace placed around a joint, as someone consented.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristlet is a band or bracelet worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Former boxing champion managed terribly old public house with parking in Italian city

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the letters are mangled
one thing in another means it is placed inside the city name

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
taken as written
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Turin is a city in northern Italy
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A boxing champion who ran an awful old pub with a car park somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside TURIN to make TURPIN. A public house is a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Randolph Turpin was the British boxer who beat Sugar Ray Robinson for the world middleweight title in 1951.

clue.text: Decorative line lights up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to light something is to fire it, as with a fuse

explanation.surface: An ornamental line that illuminates things.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small decorative stroke finishing off a letter in many typefaces.

clue.text: Lunatics he disturbed in Cape Canaveral?

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Madmen being upset somewhere at the Florida space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral in Florida is an example of a place from which rockets are fired into space.

clue.text: Ken's theory about a group of islands off Scotland

definitions.text: a group of islands off Scotland

indicators.note: about suggests turning things round and around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Ken has an idea concerning some Scottish islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orkneys are an archipelago lying off the north coast of mainland Scotland.

clue.text: Brood, remaining as a burden, do nothing

blocks.note: a broody hen sits on her eggs
something left on one's hands is a burden that remains with you

explanation.surface: Someone sulking about a lingering worry and not lifting a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brood' looks like the mood of sulking, but here it is what a hen does on her nest.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit on one's hands is an idiom for failing to act when action is needed.

clue.text: Playing harp, noisier churchgoer

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are fooled about with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worshipper making a din on the harp during the service.
explanation.definitionFit: A parishioner is a member of a parish who attends its church.

clue.text: Operate combine without starter key

indicators.note: without the key that starts it means the opening letter of the word is lost

blocks.note: to fuse things is to combine them

explanation.surface: Driving a combine harvester with no ignition key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' reads as the farm machine but is a verb here; the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To use a machine is to work or operate it.

clue.text: Guide not skating with right person in the Air Force

blocks.note: a pilot guides ships into harbour
a skater who is not skating is off the ice
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A guide who is off the rink, accompanied by a suitable airman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilot officer is the lowest commissioned rank in the Royal Air Force.

clue.text: What may be said before a meal in tip-top beanery's not half funny

definitions.text: What may be said before a meal

indicators.note: keeping not half of the word means half its letters are cut away
funny means peculiar or odd, so the letters are rearranged strangely

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen ignored
taken as written; eight letters, so half is four

explanation.surface: Something odd is said before dinner in a first-class cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of 'beanery's' is kept, and a beanery is slang for a cheap restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon appetit is the French wish for a good meal, said to diners as they begin eating.

clue.text: Consider cautious

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to think over carefully
second meaning: an adjective, careful and unhurried

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for weighing a matter up and an adjective for acting with careful intent.

clue.text: Herb used by Egon, or a rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook named Egon flavours with a herb, or perhaps with rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a Mediterranean culinary herb, often used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Tool boy singles out

blocks.note: a pick is a tool for breaking ground
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A tool-wielding lad chooses a few to set apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick on someone is to single them out, usually for unfair treatment.

clue.text: Partner in company left association

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
L is the abbreviation for left
a league is an association or alliance

explanation.surface: A business partner quit the firm's trade body.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow worker or associate, someone you partner in work.

clue.text: Fancy Elaine ringing bishop in Kansas City?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are reworked
ringing means encircling, so the name goes around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a woman called Elaine phoning a clergyman from a Kansas town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb of desire but is the anagram signal; B sits inside AILENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilene is a city in Kansas, famous as a cattle-drive railhead; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Lots excited by play of Russian writer

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: Many people were thrilled by a drama by a Russian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests a stage drama, but it is the verb toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.

clue.text: Urge wards to prosecute

blocks.note: to press someone is to urge them
people in your care are your wards or charges

explanation.surface: Encouraging people in one's care to take someone to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To press charges is to bring a formal accusation and have someone prosecuted.

clue.text: Spar with small dainty person? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sprite is an elf or fairy, small and dainty

explanation.surface: Fighting with a petite person, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' looks like a verb for boxing practice, but it is the noun for a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a spar running diagonally to support a fore-and-aft sail.

clue.text: Top English horror film

blocks.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
E is the abbreviation for English
horror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: Praise for the best British scary movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horror film' reads as one phrase, but horror is wordplay and film alone is the definition; the film is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Fear is a thriller, filmed in 1962 and remade by Martin Scorsese in 1991.

clue.text: See 22
Duck left out for a meal

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for that direction is taken away

blocks.note: a teal is a small duck
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A duck has been set aside for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' could be the verb to dodge, but it is the bird. In Britain tea can mean an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon meal, or in much of Britain the main evening meal.

clue.text: Candidate managing to win at chess

blocks.note: running a business is managing it
checkmate, shortened to mate, wins a chess game

explanation.surface: A contender handling things well enough to triumph at chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A running mate is a candidate for the lesser office, such as vice-president, on a joint ticket.

clue.text: Written work in stand is essayist's first

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them
taken as written
the opening letter of essayist's

explanation.surface: A literary piece on display is the essayist's earliest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' suggests a display stand, but it means to pay for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work dealing systematically with a subject.

clue.text: Awfully remote, it appears as a streak of light

definitions.text: it appears as a streak of light

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something terribly far away shows itself as a flash across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor, or shooting star, is a space rock burning up and seen as a bright streak across the night sky.
